result:
Solution 2 gives the correct answer, $f(n)=\frac{n+6}{5}$. This matches my recollection of the sharp result for rainbow $C_4$ in edge-colored triangle-free graphs, though I did not verify the full upper-bound proof.

The construction in Solution 2 checks out. In the $C_5$ blow-up with classes of size $n/5$ and each vertex's own color on its incoming edges, every 4-cycle repeats a color, and each vertex has color degree $\lfloor n/5\rfloor+1$. For $n\equiv 4 \pmod 5$ this is $\frac{n+1}{5}$, so $\frac{n+6}{5}$ is the smallest threshold that could be sharp there. Since $\frac{n+6}{5}$ is an integer when $n\equiv 4 \pmod 5$, the bound is consistent with integer color degrees.

Solution 1's $\frac{n+7}{5}$ is one too large. Solution 3's $\frac{n+1}{3}$ does not fit the $C_5$-type extremal structure and comes from an unverified recollection.

CHOICE: 2
